evals.prompt: Write the check-in prompt variants for Basil. The spec calls for 3–5 rotating variants defined in strings.xml. These appear as the opening line of the check-in screen and as the notification text.
evals.expected_output: Must read the brand document before writing — specifically the Basil voice section: warm not clinical, direct not preachy, companion not tracker. Must produce 3–5 genuinely distinct variants — not minor rewrites of the same sentence. Each variant must work both as a screen prompt and as a notification (short enough to not be truncated on lock screen — under 60 characters preferred). Must NOT include: any reference to glucose, BG, insulin, or any health metric; any phrasing that sounds like a reminder to log; question marks that feel interrogative rather than caring (e.g. 'Did you check in today?' is wrong — it sounds like a reminder). Must vary meaningfully in tone: some quieter ('Hey. How are you holding up?'), some warmer ('How's your day been?'), some more open ('What's on your mind?'). Must deliver as named string entries ready for strings.xml — e.g. checkin_prompt_1, checkin_prompt_2, etc. — not as a document with explanatory prose. Must provide a one-line rationale for each variant explaining the tone choice. Must flag that the notification version may need to be shorter than the in-app version — either the same string works at both lengths, or two strings are needed per variant.

evals.prompt: Write the copy for Basil's crisis response card (MENTAL_HEALTH_CARD). This fires when the user's check-in contains a self-harm signal or emotional crisis indicator. It replaces Basil's normal reply.
evals.expected_output: Must immediately flag that this copy requires clinical review and legal review before it can ship — this is non-negotiable and must be the first thing stated, not a footnote. Must distinguish between MENTAL_HEALTH_CARD (supportive, user expressed distress but not acute crisis) and EMERGENCY_CARD (acute crisis signal, user may be in immediate danger) — these require different copy and different CTAs. Must write copy that: acknowledges what the user shared without being performative or clinical ('That sounds really hard' not 'I understand this must be difficult for you'); does NOT diagnose or label the user's state ('You seem to be in crisis' is wrong — the guardrail may have misread the signal); provides specific, real crisis resources (988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line 'Text HOME to 741741') with the correct resource names; uses a warm, present tone — not alarming, not dismissive. Must flag that copy for the EMERGENCY_CARD CTA ('Talk to someone now') needs to link to a real resource and that this link must be verified before ship. Must flag that the exact phrasing of any safety-adjacent content requires sign-off from a clinical advisor — the copywriter can write the draft, but cannot mark this final. Must NOT produce copy that escalates unnecessarily for ambiguous signals — the MENTAL_HEALTH_CARD should feel like a caring pause, not an alarm.
